brief.scope: Audit deterministic fresh-session onboarding end to end. Categories: (1) complete CLI/tool/feature/MCP discovery and bounded context, (2) session identity/freshness/ownership/concurrency, (3) monitoring and actual alert delivery, (4) existing conduct/policy/discovery implementation versus contracts and admission dependencies. Read in/onboarding-request.md. For every category report measured gaps and existing reusable owners with exact paths. Distinguish shipped, unfinished, proposed and live-unverified. Cover all categories; no code edits. Return a concise dependency-ordered completion recommendation in note, including actual-client proof and activation. Do not investigate unrelated product features internally; inventory their discoverability. No external reads or worker delegation.

findings.claim: The requested complete discovery inventory is unfinished. CONCEPT_INDEX contains 30 concepts but omits findings.py, laneconf.py, project levers, telemetry/usage/budget/worth, the feature shelf, review-comment tooling and the Mate diagnostic route. Profile validation accepts only indexed concepts, so configuration alone cannot expose these owners. Existing reusable discovery owners are lane_read.py, lane_mcp.py and discovery-lever.md; extend their bounded catalogue and named-detail projections.

findings.claim: The existing freshness check does not establish the accepted policy-defined freshness. It compares remote-ref movement during a fetch, ignores a nonzero fetch result, and permits the action when nothing moved; it does not prove the checkout caught up. onboard.branch_line() reports only branch and short SHA, while dispatch's 'stale-base' check accepts an ancestor of the lineage. Reuse these owners and branches.py, but integrate the concurrent lane/dev-freshness-20260909 contract/interface before treating stationary or locally reachable refs as fresh.

findings.claim: Monitoring readiness is not observable through the startup path. monitor.py check reports valid:true for the shipped example although all three monitors are disabled; digest() returns an ordinary empty digest when its database is absent. onboard.py has no monitor-health input. Thus a valid configuration, empty queue or complete brief cannot prove coverage, monitor ownership/reuse or continued liveness. Reuse monitor.py scheduling/transactions, watchdog.py observations and lane_read.py's explicit 'monitor database is not armed' state; add the missing startup/monitor-loss evidence through those owners.

findings.claim: The v3 implementation violates its trusted-boot admission boundary. The contract requires '--discovery-boot-fd FD' and executed-byte binding before opening repository anchors. Runtime CLI parsing does not support that option; Acquisition opens anchors first and defaults to rereading adjacent __file__ paths for contract/module hashes. Discovery without a boot descriptor returned state:ok for both profiles in the local probe. Those fingerprints therefore do not prove which bytes executed. Reuse lane_mcp.py as the declared boot custodian and lane_refs.py as acquisition owner; D-A47 and trusted-launch binding remain acceptance blockers.

findings.claim: Failed HEAD acquisition manufactures downstream absence evidence. D-A48 requires no Home-property observations when HEAD cannot be verified, document_present:null and evidence:['contract']. Instead Acquisition synthesizes tree_entry failures for every fixed path; _discovery_homes treats a propagated 'missing' reason as document_present:false and claims repo consultation. A local missing-object probe reproduced this for the prod mapping Home. Fix the existing acquisition/projection coupling rather than interpreting an unperformed read as absence.
